divebooker.note: divebooker.com states a fare on every departure and this dataset now publishes them, on the sailings it lists and nowhere else. What the withholding was waiting on was the currency: it comes from the page's own payload rather than from `Offer.priceCurrency`, which is a static per-vessel label that does not describe `Offer.price`, and read that way 725 of 777 joined sailings carry a figure identical to one of the other two sellers'. The 52 that do not are three sellers disagreeing about a berth, which is what this page draws — and they concentrate rather than scatter: twelve are Unity's whole season at a steady 1.43x. One row stands alone, Red Sea Aggressor IV on 2027-07-24 at exactly twice the other two for the same seven nights, and it is printed as the seller states it rather than dropped, because deleting a published price is the failure this site reports in other people. Of 945 in-season sailing(s), 786 land on a row one of the other two sellers founded, keyed on (boat, date), and 87 are rows this seller founded itself, on a date or a hull the other two do not list, and 15 sit on hull(s) the alias map does not know, so nothing can be said about them, and 57 reach no row at all, every one of them because this seller states no fare for that date — a route on request is an enquiry and not a berth anybody priced. See docs/divebooker-limitations.md.

berths_note: departures[].berths is one block per seller: [seller index into sellers, places left at the advertised price, [cabins], berths left on the sailing, and -- only where it is not berths_read -- the day that seller's ladder was read]. Each cabin is [name index into cabin_names, price per person in the display currency, places left (0 = full, null = not stated), single-occupancy surcharge %]. Both counts are totals -- the first across every room selling at the advertised price, the second across every room at any price -- and either is null where any room it covers does not state a count, because one unstated figure makes the sum unknown rather than partial. The two are different claims and are never merged: PADI Travel publishes only the second, and it was measured against liveaboard.com's rather than assumed (77% exact, 88% within two berths, against 22% for the count at the advertised price). A seller that publishes a count but no ladder has a null cabin list: 24 places and 24 places at a stated price are different claims, and only the second is a ladder.
